channel.title: From the Edit Bay — Rushikesh Jadhav
channel.description: Case studies, behind-the-scenes stories, editing tips, and creative thoughts from a cinematic video editor in Pune, India.

image.title: From the Edit Bay — Rushikesh Jadhav

item.title: How we made Licious feel like cinema — not just an ad
item.description: The brief was simple: show why Licious is premium. The challenge was avoiding every tired food-video cliché. Here's the frame-by-frame thinking behind the grade, the pacing, and why we cut 40 seconds the client loved.

item.title: Shooting a corporate film in a live factory — what nobody tells you
item.description: Astik Dyestuff gave us 6 hours, one shift, and no second chance. Here's how we mapped audio, light, and b-roll in a chemical plant.

item.title: How I open every SaaS demo video — and why most get it wrong
item.description: After editing the Bible Notes app demo and three other SaaS products, a pattern emerged. Here's the 3-second rule I now follow.

item.title: Luxury real estate film — Wakad project walkthrough
item.description: The brief asked for aspirational. We delivered cinematic. A look at how aerial + interior work together when the property sells a lifestyle, not just a flat.

item.title: Are Indian D2C brands ready for cinematic video?
item.description: After working with food, fashion, and SaaS brands across Pune and Mumbai, a clear split is emerging — and it's not about budget.

item.title: Brand film vs. corporate film — why my DaVinci Resolve node tree changes
item.description: Same LUT, same footage, two different storytelling goals. Here's how my DaVinci Resolve node tree changes between the two.

item.title: Product table-top shoots — 6 shots that made the final cut vs 40 that didn't
item.description: Table-top product films look simple. They're not. A look at the lighting rig, lens choices, and the 6 shots that made the final cut vs the 40 that didn't.

item.title: Why I always record room tone — and 4 other habits that save hours in post
item.description: Small habits compound. Room tone, slate discipline, color charts, proxy workflows — the boring stuff that separates amateurs from professionals.

item.title: Bible Notes app — motion graphics demo that took 200+ layers
item.description: A clean, minimal demo that looks effortless. Behind it: 200+ After Effects layers, Element 3D, and a Figma-to-motion pipeline that took weeks to refine.
